title: Anchored request seals: server-backed idempotent tokens for billing safety
creator: Maya Thompson
description:
Background: We continue to see sporadic duplicate charges surface when clients retry requests across flaky mobile networks and multi-homed edge proxies. Existing strategies (client-generated nonces and short-lived request IDs) reduce duplicates but fail when retries cross proxies or after transient failovers.

Proposal: Implement a server-backed "anchored request seal" system. Instead of trusting only a client-supplied idempotency key, the edge ingress will obtain a short-lived anchor seal from a centralized Anchor Service. The seal is an HMAC-signed blob that encodes: customer_id, model_variant, token_quota_snapshot, and a monotonically increasing anchor_epoch. Anchors are cheap to mint and held in an in-memory lease table. When the ingress observes a retry or a multi-segment request, it attaches the anchor seal to the ingestion record. Billing boundary enforcement will only charge when the seal has been consumed against the customer ledger once.

Design details: 1) Anchor lifecycle - anchors are valid for a tunable window (default 2 minutes). They can be renewed if the client shows forward progress (e.g., partial tokens consumed). 2) Lease semantics - the Anchor Service manages soft leases with epoch numbers to prevent replay across restarts. 3) Consumption semantics - payment events are only emitted when the anchor's consumption record transitions from "reserved" to "finalized." Duplicate consumption requests with the same anchor are deduped via a single-commit reconciliation path. 4) Fallback - if Anchor Service is unreachable, ingress falls back to conservative local reservation semantics (reserve tokens but delay final invoicing until reconciliation).

Trade-offs considered: - Strong centralization of anchors simplifies global dedupe but introduces an availability dependency; mitigated by short leases, local reservation fallback, and multi-region Anchor replicas. - Anchor metadata increases ingress message size; we limit payload to a compact binary HMAC. - Reconciliation path must handle eventual consistency when anchors are renewed or failover occurs; introduced background sweeper to reconcile partial anchors.

Rollout plan: 1) Implement Anchor Service and ingress hooks behind a feature flag. 2) Canary on internal teams with low-volume workloads for 48 hours. 3) Enable for a subset of customers with explicit opt-in and audit logging. 4) Monitor duplicate-billing-rate, invoice delta, and latency impact. 5) Gradual ramp to general availability with an emergency rollback path to delay final invoicing by 24 hours.

Metrics and observability: - metric: billing.duplicate_attempts_per_1k_requests, billing.anchors_minted_per_minute, billing.anchor_reconciliations_failed, latency.ingress.auth_anchor_hop. Dashboards and an alert runbook will accompany the rollout.

Test plan: unit tests for HMAC creation/validation, integration tests for lease handoff, chaos test for Anchor Service failover and ingress fallback, and billing e2e tests that simulate retried multi-hop requests.

Expected outcome: Significant reduction in confirmed duplicate charges for retried requests (target: 90% reduction for cross-proxy retries) while adding minimal tail latency (target: <8ms median added at ingress).
acceptance_criteria: Anchor Service can mint and validate seals with <5ms median latency in-region
Ingress attaches and validates anchors and falls back to local reservation when anchor service is unreachable
Billing ledger receives exactly-once finalize events for sealed requests in canary and pilot customers
Monitoring dashboards show duplicate-billing-rate reduced by >=50% during pilot
Comprehensive tests (unit, integration, chaos) in CI with coverage for renewal and reconciliation paths
implementation_notes: API: /anchors/mint (POST) => {customer_id, model_hint, quota_snapshot} returns base64seal and epoch. Anchors are HMAC-signed with KMS-managed key. Lease table stores epoch -> (seal, reserved_tokens, status). Consumption endpoint accepts anchor + consumption delta; it performs idempotent apply using high-watermark commit. Reconciliation job sweeps leases marked RESERVED older than 5 minutes, queries ingress logs, and finalizes or rolls back reservations. Add opt-in flag on tenant config with telemetry to measure impact. Keep Anchor Service stateless for horizontal scaling; use region-local in-memory caches with cross-region replication for high availability. Store final consumption events in the existing consumption-ledger topic for downstream billing.
